newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Telstra sets up at Asia Internet links.
newsitem.headline: Telstra sets up at Asia Internet links.

text.p: Australian telephone carrier Telstra Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it had formed Internet agreements with a several Asian countries including Singapore, Japan, South Korea and Hong Kong.
Telstra said the agreements will result in reduced reliance on the United States and lower operating costs.

Telstra was championing a change to the Internet commercial arrangements for all non-U.S. Internet operators, particularly in the Asia Pacific region, Telstra managing director for International Carrier Business John Hibbard said in a statement.
"As a consequence of the existing regime, International Service Providers in Asia need to charge higher prices than those in the USA," Hibbard said.
"Telstra is concerned that this could negatively impact the growth of the Internet," he said.

"Furthermore, the high costs associated with service to the USA will discourage the expansion transmission capacity to the USA, so impacting upon the quality of servie available to Asian users," he added.
Hibbard said Telstra has been pursuing a change in arrangements with the United States through U.S. operators and the U.S. Federal Communications Commisssion (FCC).
